title: The Million-Person Evacuation
record_caveat: This is the success case, and its record is thinner than the US and Spanish inquiries. There is no public inquiry. The sources are IMD's own report on the storm (primary: bulletin times, forecasts, radar, tolls as supplied by the state), the joint Government of Odisha / World Bank / Asian Development Bank damage assessment, a slide presentation by an OSDMA chief general manager (undated), and three press reports. The Odisha government's own order-by-order timeline was not fetchable, so the record does not say at what hour any evacuation order was given, and most of the evacuation (the 36 hours before landfall) began on 11 October, before this clock opens. The clock is a single day because the game cannot cross midnight. Where an item comes from an undated source it is placed by plausibility and says so in its text. The IMD report stamps its warning bulletins in a day-hour-minute form with an unexplained suffix (for example 120630ef); they are read here as IST. The landfall hour varies inside IMD's own report (about 21:30 IST in its satellite section, 22:30 in its summary; radar shows the eye over land by 22:05) and in press (about 21:15). Wind figures are not comparable across agencies: IMD reports 3-minute winds, the US Joint Typhoon Warning Center 1-minute winds. Where this scenario cannot say what a different decision would have caused, it says so: the record is silent on every path not taken. The score is game design, not a claim about lives saved. The scoring field for the first public alert is set to the first listed bulletin of this day, 06:30, only because the clock cannot hold the real first alerts of 8 to 10 October.

info_available.text: IMD raised its landfall wind forecast in yesterday's 08:30 bulletin: gale winds of 210-220 kmph along and off the coastal districts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha at landfall. Its forecast of the morning of 9 October had said 175-185 kmph, gusting to 200. Landfall is forecast near Gopalpur, by night of the 12th.

citation.detail: Section 9, items (iv) and (v), and Table 12 (bulletin of 11.10.13, 0830 IST)

info_available.text: IMD's storm-surge forecast of 17:30 yesterday: a surge of 3.0 to 3.5 m above the astronomical tide, flooding the low-lying areas of Ganjam, Khurda, Puri and Jagatsinghpur districts of Odisha and Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh at landfall. The forecast of 17:30 on 10 October had said around 1.5 to 2.0 m.

Press reports of the day carry a second number. The US Navy's Joint Typhoon Warning Center forecasts maximum sustained winds of 269 kph with gusts up to 315 kph. A weather presenter says: 'There are some discrepancies in terms of the forecast. The Indian forecasts are slightly different from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.' Some foreign forecasters are suggesting that India's weather office is underestimating the storm.

citation.detail: Al Jazeera, 'Cyclone Phailin hits India's east coast', 12 Oct 2013: the JTWC forecast, the presenter's remark and the report of foreign forecasters' view. Article time of day not stated

info_available.text: IMD's Bhubaneswar warning centre has issued cyclone watch (from 8 October), alert (from 9 October) and warning (from 10 October) bulletins; the same time stamps appear in its list of press, All India Radio and Doordarshan/TV bulletins. Fishermen warnings have gone out since 21:30 on 8 October. From 06:30 today the port signal is GD-X at Gopalpur and Puri and GD-IX at Paradip and Chandbali.

citation.detail: Section 8.2 (Cyclone Warning Centre Bhubaneswar): watch, alert, warning, press/AIR/Doordarshan, fishermen and port-warning lists

options.label: One voice: every public message carries IMD's forecast
options.detail: Radio bulletins, public appeals and district orders all rest on IMD's numbers. The foreign estimate stays out of the messaging.

consequence.text: This is what happened: the state's warnings rested on IMD's forecast ('accurate early warning by IMD' heads OSDMA's list of what went right), were repeated on All India Radio every 15 minutes, and the Chief Minister appealed to the public not to panic and to co-operate with the administration.

citation.detail: Slides '10 front preparedness' (item 1) and 'Continuous Govt.-public interface'

options.label: Lead public messaging with the foreign Category-5 estimate
options.detail: Tell the coast that the US Navy's Joint Typhoon Warning Center expects stronger winds than IMD, and warn for that.

options.label: No new message today: the evacuation order is out, leave it there
options.detail: People have had days of warnings. Add nothing, change nothing.

historical_citation.detail: Slides 'Early warning' (single authority) and '10 front preparedness' (accurate early warning by IMD)

info_available.text: IMD's track puts the centre at 18.1N, 85.7E at 11:30 (06:00 UTC), moving northwest at about 15 kmph, with sustained winds of 115 knots (215 kmph) and a central pressure of 940 hPa. The Visakhapatnam radar, watching since 06:30, shows an almost closed eye about 30 km across.

citation.detail: Table 1 (best track, 12-10-2013 0600 UTC), Table 3 row 8 (DWR Visakhapatnam, 0600z) and Section 2.2

info_available.text: Ganjam's most senior civil servant, Krishan Kumar, has not slept for three nights, setting up hundreds of temporary shelters in schools and temples and persuading villagers to leave flimsy homes. 'The weather was very good, the sun was shining and to convince people was not an easy job.' He has asked to be authorised to decide at his own level, and has told officials across Ganjam to act as they see fit, including keeping village shops open so supplies are not hoarded. (The record gives no hour for his account.)

citation.detail: Reuters, 'In the eye of a storm: How Indian bureaucrats got it right', section 'Empowering local officials'

info_available.text: Mobile phones are a tool the state did not have in 1999: Kumar says he is able to reach officials in remote villages by phone to spread word of the coming storm. About 25 million people in Odisha, 60% of the state's population, carry a phone. (The record gives no hour for this.)

citation.detail: Reuters, same article: district chief Kumar on mobile phones; 25 million users, 60% of the state's population

options.label: Let district officials use force on people who refuse to leave
options.detail: The order is out and the law allows force. Tell the districts to use it where persuasion has failed.

consequence.text: This is what happened: Section 34(C) of the Disaster Management Act 2005 was promulgated, empowering the district administration to use force if required for evacuation.

options.label: Persuasion only: no force, however long the holdouts take
options.detail: Keep sending officials and volunteers village to village, and ask nothing of those who still refuse.

options.label: Stop pressing the holdouts: they have had days of warnings
options.detail: Whoever is still in a flimsy house has chosen. Put the effort into the shelters instead.

historical_citation.detail: Slide 'Preparing for combat': Section 34(C) of the Disaster Management Act 2005 promulgated, empowering the district administration to use force if required for evacuation

info_available.text: IMD's 17:30 storm-surge forecast holds at 3.0 to 3.5 m above the astronomical tide, flooding the low-lying areas of Ganjam, Khurda, Puri and Jagatsinghpur at landfall. Model guidance from INCOIS and IIT Delhi gives a surge of 2 to 3 m; the IIT Bhubaneswar model gives 3.5 m.

citation.detail: Table 13 (forecast of 12.10.13/1730) and Section 7.6 (storm surge guidance)

The black wedge is the gap between two satellite swaths, not cloud or smoke. A satellite picture, not a wind or surge measurement.

info_available.text: The state's public line, as OSDMA later described it: warnings on All India Radio every 15 minutes, in the commonly used language; an appeal from the Chief Minister not to panic and to co-operate with the administration; and the Special Relief Commissioner, through the media, asking the public to co-operate with the government on evacuation. (The record gives no hour for this.)

The shelters are ready: OSDMA has run mock drills at all the cyclone shelters and checked or replaced their equipment; the cyclone and flood shelter management committees are activated to help move the vulnerable; all 14 cyclone-prone districts hold satellite phones in case the phone lines fail; free kitchens have been open since 11 October. Government employees' Dussehra holidays are cancelled.

options.label: Hold the order as issued and keep the shelters filling
options.detail: Everyone in low-lying areas, and in flimsy houses within 10 km of the coast, goes to a shelter or a safe building, as already ordered.

consequence.text: This is what happened: the order stood. All people living in low-lying areas and in kutcha or tin-roof houses within 0-10 km of the coastline were ordered to nearby cyclone shelters or other identified safe buildings, and over 1 million people were evacuated within 36 hours preceding landfall.

options.label: Widen the order: move people from beyond the 10 km line too
options.detail: The surge forecast has risen. Bring in people from further inland before dark.

options.label: Declare the evacuation complete: stop moving people
options.detail: Those who have not come by now will not come. Close admission to the shelters and prepare to shelter in place.

historical_citation.detail: Section 1.3, paragraph 13 (the 0-10 km order and the evacuation in the 36 hours before landfall)

info_available.text: IMD's 20:30 cyclone warning is out. The Visakhapatnam radar measured winds of 60 m/s at 4 km height at 19:40 (14:10 UTC) with an eye 18 km across. IMD's track puts the centre at 19.1N, 85.2E at 20:30 (15:00 UTC), still at 115 knots and 940 hPa, heading for a landfall near Gopalpur.

citation.detail: Table 3 row 16 and Section 4.2 (DWR Visakhapatnam); Table 1 (12-10-2013 1500 UTC); Section 8.2 (warning at 122030)

info_available.text: In Ganjam, with a couple of hours to go before landfall, some 350,000 people living up to 10 km from the shoreline are in shelters for the night.

citation.detail: Reuters, same article: 'With a couple of hours to go before the storm made landfall, some 350,000 people living up to 10 km (6 miles) from the shoreline were safely sheltered for the night'

info_available.text: Teams and stock are in position. Odisha's rapid-action force, the state fire service and the national disaster-response force are deployed with equipment at strategic locations; tracks are assigned to teams for clearing the relief lines; seven days of food, fuel and relief materials are prepositioned; satellite phones are with the vulnerable districts as the last line of communication. (The record gives no hour for this.)

options.label: Keep the teams prepositioned and clear the roads once the cyclone abates
options.detail: Control rooms stay open; response teams, equipment and relief stock stay where they are placed.

consequence.text: This is what happened: major roads were cleared within 24 hours, and about 5.7 MT of dry food was airdropped by IAF helicopters to inaccessible areas.

options.label: Send crews onto the coast roads now, ahead of the wind
options.detail: Put teams out to reach anyone still moving toward the shelters before the eye arrives.

options.label: Stand the control rooms down for the night and resume at first light
options.detail: Nothing more can be done until the wind drops. Rest the staff.

historical_citation.detail: Slides 'Preparing for combat' (prepositioning, relief-line clearance plans) and 'Milestones' (restoration of road communication within 12-24 hours of abatement)

historical_path.action: The state kept to IMD's forecast as the single early warning, repeated on All India Radio every 15 minutes, with the Chief Minister's appeal not to panic. The record does not say whether the Joint Typhoon Warning Center's higher numbers were discussed.

citation.detail: Slides 'Early warning', '10 front preparedness' and 'Continuous Govt.-public interface'

historical_path.action: Section 34(C) of the Disaster Management Act 2005 was promulgated, empowering the district administration to use force if required for evacuation.

The 0-10 km order stood: all people in low-lying areas and in kutcha or tin-roof houses within 0-10 km of the coastline to nearby cyclone shelters or other safe buildings. Over 1 million people were evacuated within 36 hours before landfall.
Response teams stayed prepositioned with their equipment; major roads were cleared within 24 hours of the cyclone and IAF helicopters airdropped dry food to cut-off areas.

inquiry_findings.quote: Preparedness of the Government of Odisha (GoO) and the coastal communities and their resolve to ensure zero casualties resulted in prompt action to the warning of the cyclone.

citation.detail: Executive Summary, paragraph 2 (joint Government of Odisha, World Bank and ADB assessment; there was no public inquiry)

inquiry_findings.quote: To ensure zero casualties, the GoO ordered all people living in low lying areas and kutcha houses or tin roof houses within 0-10 km of the coastline to be evacuated to nearby cyclone shelters or other identified safe buildings.
Single authority for EW or people may act on incorrect or misleading information
inquiry_findings.translation: OSDMA's own slide on early warning (EW): one authority should issue the warning, or people may act on wrong information.

inquiry_findings.quote: After the 1999 super cyclone, the state government has taken measures like the installation of modern communication systems, construction of cyclone shelters, and other improved infrastructure

Compliance with the evacuation order was high but uneven. In some areas as many as 95% of residents left; in others as few as 33% did. Unemployment, theft and no provision for evacuating livestock to safety explained the failures to leave significantly.

citation.detail: Abstract, Climatic Change 152:291-305 (peer-reviewed study of evacuation responses to Phailin in Odisha's coastal districts)

inquiry_findings.quote: The forecasters' own numbers differ by agency and by averaging period. In the archive's reanalysis the US Joint Typhoon Warning Center has Phailin at 140 knots (1-minute winds, Category 5 on the Saffir-Simpson scale) at its peak on 11 and 12 October; IMD has 115 knots (3-minute winds). The archive says it makes no adjustment for differing averaging periods, so the two figures cannot be read straight across.

citation.detail: IBTrACS v04r01, storm 2013281N12098: USA_WIND and WMO_WIND columns, 11-12 Oct 2013; column documentation on averaging periods

takeaways.text: When forecasters disagree, the desk can still speak with one voice: OSDMA's own lesson is that a single authority for early warning stops people acting on incorrect or misleading information.
An order that names who must move and how far from the sea can be carried out village by village: here, low-lying areas and flimsy houses within 0-10 km of the coast.
Shelters and communications built after the 1999 super cyclone were already in place when Phailin came; the evacuation was a matter of using them, not building them.

deaths.note: Counts differ by what they include. 21 were killed by the cyclone itself (IMD's report, as supplied by the state; OSDMA). The floods that followed add 17 in IMD's report and 23 in OSDMA's table, and the joint damage assessment gives 44 dead in all. IMD lists one further death in coastal Andhra Pradesh. Press counts were 25 on 14 October (AP) and 21 on 16 October (Reuters). For comparison, the 1999 super cyclone is given as 'about 10,000' dead in the damage assessment, as 8,900 in OSDMA's comparison table, and as 8,243 in a government report quoted by Al Jazeera; this scenario does not resolve those to one figure. Evacuation is graded the same way: the state's own tally is 983,642 for the cyclone (and 171,083 more for the floods that followed), the damage assessment says 'over 1 million' within 36 hours, and the 1.2 million sometimes quoted rests on secondary summaries only.

citation.detail: Executive Summary, paragraph 1 ('left 44 people dead'). The other figures in the note come from the IMD report (section 6.1), the OSDMA slides 'Phailin and floods' and 'Super cyclone 1999 vs Phailin 2013', and the press reports named

minutes_matter.quote: Disaster-related mortality is nearly six times lower in countries with more comprehensive Multi-Hazard Early Warning System capabilities compared to countries with limited capabilities.
minutes_matter.about: Every country that reports on its warning systems
minutes_matter.caveat: A cross-country association, not a measured effect: richer countries tend to have both more warning capability and lower mortality.
